cues.en: In the last video, we talked about the beginnings of JPEG. So what do we do at the beginning of the process to start preparing for the discrete cosine transform, which is really how the lossy compression happens within a JPEG
cues.zh: 在上一期视频中，我们聊了 JPEG 的起源。那么在这个流程的开头，我们做什么来为离散余弦变换做准备——JPEG 里的有损压缩实际上就是靠它完成的

cues.en: compressed file. So,
cues.zh: 压缩文件。所以，

cues.zh: 我们从 RGB 图像开始。把它转换成 YCBCR

cues.en: Before we start talking about how images are compressed using the discrete cosine transform, it's much better just to start with a simple example of what a discrete cosine transform is and how it works. A cosine function, for anyone that isn't familiar with it, is a function that goes between one and minus one. What we tend to do on this on this x axis is go from naught to pi to two pi. This is in radians. Those of you familiar with degrees, this is a 180 degrees at pi and 360
cues.zh: 在开始讲图像如何用离散余弦变换压缩之前，最好先从一个简单例子入手，看看离散余弦变换是什么、怎么工作。余弦函数，如果有人不熟悉，就是一个在 1 和 -1 之间变化的函数。我们在这条 x 轴上通常从 0 到 π 再到 2π。这是弧度。熟悉角度的人知道，π 对应 180 度，360

cues.zh: 度对应 2π。余弦波看起来是这样。它在 0 处为 1，然后在 π 处

cues.zh: 在 2π 处。随着你继续增大，它就这样一直上下起伏。离散余弦变换的工作方式是：我们取一些数据，这里是图像数据，

So let's imagine that we've got this cosine wave here, which is our standard frequency cosine wave, and then we've got another cosine wave, which is a much higher frequency.

cues.en: So that will be come down a bit faster,
cues.zh: 所以它下降得会快一点，

cues.en: go up a bit faster, come down a bit faster, and go up a bit faster like this. Okay? So now we have two waves. If we add them together, what we get is a sort of another wave, which is a combination of the two. So if we draw in here in this dash line,
cues.zh: 上升快一点，下降快一点，再上升快一点，像这样。对吧？现在有两个波。把它们相加，得到的是另一种波，是两个波的组合。所以如果我们在这里用虚线画出来，

cues.zh: 可以看到两个波中间的位置是这样，

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: as we increase the number of cosines, we can increase the number of possible shapes of waves that we can produce. In practice, if we added these two waves together, we'd have a wave that was much taller than the input. So here, it would be two, not one. So what in fact we do is we weight both of these, and so we take an average. So both of these are weighted, in this case, as a half, and so this is essentially the average of both of them. We could also change the weighting of these. So we could have it with mostly this high frequency one, but only a little bit of this low frequency one, and we'd have a different shaped wave coming out the end. So each wave represents
cues.zh: 随着余弦波数量增加，我们能产生的波形种类也会增加。实际上，如果直接把这两个波相加，得到的波会比输入高很多。这里会是 2，而不是 1。所以实际上我们给这两个波都加权，也就是取平均。这里两个权重都是 1/2，所以这基本上就是它们的平均值。我们也可以改变权重。比如主要用这个高频波，只加一点这个低频波，最后就会得到不同形状的波。所以每个波代表

cues.en: a small constituent of the of the output. And the higher the frequency the wave, the higher the frequency part of the signal we're dealing with. So if we look at my my jumper here, there's a low frequency change from this black table to a brightness right over my jumper to dark table again. And there's much higher frequency changes on my jumper where we go up and down within sort of the woolen knit. And it's the same kind of principle. We're arguing in JPEG that we can get rid of some of the higher frequency signals,
cues.zh: 输出的一小部分成分。波的频率越高，我们处理的就是信号中频率越高的部分。看看我身上这件毛衣：从黑色桌子到毛衣上的亮处、再回到暗色桌子，这是低频变化。而毛衣上羊毛针织的起伏里，有高得多的频率变化。原理是一样的。我们在 JPEG 中主张，可以丢掉一些高频信号，

cues.en: and the general gist of the image will still be there.
cues.zh: 而图像的整体观感仍然还在。

cues.en: So this is just a one dimensional discrete cosine transom with only two components.
cues.zh: 这只是一个仅包含两个分量的一维离散余弦变换。

cues.en: The way that the the mathematics works is if we have a signal that's eight long, then we find that we can represent it using eight cosine waves of different frequencies.
cues.zh: 其数学原理是，如果我们有一个长度为 8 的信号，就能用 8 个不同频率的余弦波来表示它。

cues.en: And the same is true of an image. What we do in JPEG is we split each image into eight by eight pixel groups, and each of those pixel groups is separately encoded with its own discrete cosine transform.
cues.zh: 图像也是同理。在 JPEG 中，我们会把每张图像拆成 8x8 的像素块，每个像素块都通过各自的离散余弦变换独立编码。

cues.en: Each of those eight by eight pixel groups can be exactly replicated by
cues.zh: 每个 8x8 的像素块都可以完全由

cues.en: 64, so eight by eight cosine waves. This actually shows the 64 base cosine waves that produce any image we might like to do in eight by eight pixels. This particular component here is essentially flat. Okay? So if you had only this component and that was all that contributed to your final output, your image would look like that. Okay? If you had only this one, your image would go white, and then it would dip down and go black. And you can see that the frequency is increasing as we go along here. This is in the x direction, and then in the y direction, the frequency is increasing
cues.zh: 64 个，也就是 8x8 个余弦波精确复原。这里展示的正是能生成任意 8x8 像素图像的 64 个基余弦波。这里的这个分量基本上是平坦的，对吧？所以如果只有这个分量对最终输出起作用，图像就会是那个样子。明白吧？如果只有这一个，图像就会先变白，然后下凹变黑。可以看到，从左到右频率在逐渐增加。这是 x 方向，而在 y 方向上，频率则是

cues.en: down here. So this is a cosine wave, and this is a higher frequency cosine wave down here. As we increase the frequency in both directions, we get a kind of checkerboard pattern. And this is a high frequency information
cues.zh: 向下逐渐增加。这是一个余弦波，下面这个则是频率更高的余弦波。当我们在两个方向上都增加频率，就会得到一种棋盘格图案。这就是高频信息，

cues.en: that we're encoding in these regions.
cues.zh: 也就是我们在这些区域编码的内容。

cues.en: So these are the 64
cues.zh: 所以这就是 64 个

cues.en: cosine functions that can be combined to make any eight by eight image.
cues.zh: 可以组合生成任意 8x8 图像的余弦函数。

cues.en: This is only in one channel. So let's say, just luminance or just CR. For example, if we had half of this wave and half of this wave, then what you get is a square of of image that was generally brighter on the left with a little bit of bright on the right hand side because you've summed the two together. To create any kind of eight by eight image, what we need to do is have a combination of all of these at the same time. Each of these is weighted
cues.zh: 这还只是单通道的情况，比如单纯的亮度通道或单纯的 Cr 通道。举个例子，如果我们取这个波的一半加上那个波的一半，得到的就是一个左边整体偏亮、右侧微亮的正方形图像，因为把两者叠加在了一起。要生成任意一种 8x8 图像，我们需要把所有这些基波同时组合起来。每个基波都会加权，

cues.en: based on something called a coefficient, which represent... Is a number representing the contribution of each of these individual
cues.zh: 权重来自所谓的“系数”，这个数值代表每个单独的

cues.en: blocks
cues.zh: 基波块

cues.en: to the whole. So for example, if the contribution of this one is zero, then there is no part of this cosine wave in the in the eight by eight image that we're looking at. If it's a naught point one and this one's 10,
cues.zh: 对整体的贡献。举个例子，如果这个分量的贡献为 0，那么在我们看的 8x8 图像中就完全没有这个余弦波的成分。如果它是 0.1 而另一个是 10，

cues.en: then this has obviously got a hundredfold less impact on your output image than this one. And what we do with discrete cosine transform
cues.zh: 那它对输出图像的影响显然比另一个小了 100 倍。而我们做离散余弦变换，

cues.en: is basically calculate the coefficients for these waves. Putting this discrete cosine transform aside for a minute, if we just look at an example image. So this is a small crop section of our flower image. This is the y component.
cues.zh: 本质上就是计算这些波的系数。先把离散余弦变换放一边，我们来看一张示例图像。这是从我们的花朵图像中裁剪出的一小块。这是 Y 分量（亮度分量）。

cues.en: So it's just every value from naught to two five five, how intense is the pixel.
cues.zh: 所以它只是从 0 到 255 的每个值，表示这个像素有多亮。

cues.en: So you can see this is not a hugely interesting piece of image. It's kind of gray with a little bit of brighter region down here. What we want to try and do is calculate the contribution of each of our cosine waves to this image. Which bits of cosine do we need to add together
cues.zh: 所以你可以看到，这并不算一块特别有意思的图像。它偏灰，下面这里有一点更亮的区域。我们想尝试做的，是计算每个余弦波对这幅图像的贡献。我们需要把哪些余弦部分加在一起

cues.en: to create an image that looks exactly like this? So to start with, what we need to do is center all of these values, which are currently centered around a 128 because they're from naught to two five five. We center all these values around zero because, remember, a cosine wave goes from one to minus one, not from one to naught. So we take away a 128 off every value, and we get our shifted block like this. So this is the exact same image, but this time now centered around zero. And now we can use this in the discrete cosine transform to calculate our coefficients. We apply the... It's actually discrete cosine transform number two, which is the one that's always used in JPEG. And what that does is calculate the the contribution of each of our cosine waves that when added together will create this image exactly right. Which of these blocks, when multiplied by their coefficients to tell us how much of each one we use, will add together to create this exact image. So it might be a bit of that, a bit of this, a bit of that, a lot of that. Yeah. And none of this one. Exactly. And so you will find that all of these will have some impact on the image. It's almost certain unless the image is completely flat. One of the nice things about JPEG is these low frequency ones will have a much bigger effect from the high frequency data, and we also see them better. So that's how we we compress JPEG. So we calculate our d c t two coefficients,
cues.zh: 才能创建出一幅看起来完全像这样的图像？那么首先，我们需要做的是把所有这些值居中，它们目前是围绕 128 居中的，因为它们来自 0 到 255。我们把所有这些值围绕零居中，因为记住，余弦波是从 1 到 -1，而不是从 1 到 0。所以我们把每个值都减去 128，就得到这样平移后的块。所以这是完全相同的图像，但这次是围绕零居中。现在我们可以把它用于离散余弦变换来计算系数。我们应用的是……其实是第二种离散余弦变换，也就是 JPEG 里一直用的那个。它做的是计算每个余弦波的贡献，这些余弦波加在一起就能准确生成这幅图像。这些块中哪些在乘上各自的系数（告诉我们每个用多少）之后加在一起，会得到这幅完全一样的图像。所以可能是那个一点、这个一点、那个一点、那个很多。对。而这个完全不用。没错。你会发现所有这些都会对图像有影响。几乎可以肯定，除非图像完全平坦。JPEG 的一个好处是，这些低频分量比高频数据的影响大得多，而且我们也更容易看到它们。这就是我们压缩 JPEG 的方式。所以我们计算 DCT-2 系数，

cues.en: and that gives us some slightly arbitrary values between minus 1,024
cues.zh: 这会给我们一些多少有点任意的值，介于 -1024

cues.en: and plus 1,024.

But that's not too much of a big problem. And what we have, each of these represents the weight or the amount of each of our cosine waves. So if we put this next to here, we can say that if we take this cosine
cues.zh: 但这不算什么大问题。我们得到的是，每个值代表对应余弦波的权重或用量。所以如果我们把这个放到这里旁边，可以说，如果我们取这个余弦

cues.en: and multiply it by minus three seventy
and add it to this one multiplied by 29.7
cues.zh: 把它加到这一项上，这一项乘以 29.7

cues.en: and so on, and we do it for all of them, the added sum will be our original image back again. Usually,
cues.zh: 以此类推，对所有这些都这样做，加总起来就会重新得到原始图像。通常，

cues.en: this top left coefficient is much bigger than the others because this... Because it's a flat and it's actually flat and not a cosine way, represents the general intensity of that particular image block. So this is called our direct current coefficient or DC coefficient.
cues.zh: 左上角这个系数比其他系数大得多，因为这个……因为它是一个平坦分量，实际是平的，不是余弦波，代表那个图像块的整体强度。所以这被称为我们的直流系数，或 DC 系数。

cues.en: All of the others are alternating current, AC coefficients. In practice, usually, the DC coefficients are stored separately, but we, you know, we won't we won't dwell on that too much. The really important aspect of JPEG that you need... You want to understand is that these coefficients are often very, very small, and these ones are very, very big. And what that tells us is that the high frequency
cues.zh: 其余的都是交流，也就是 AC 系数。实际中，直流系数通常会单独存储，不过我们……你知道，我们不会……不会在这上面讲太多。JPEG 里你真正需要……你需要理解的重要一点是，这些系数往往非常非常小，而这些又非常非常大。这告诉我们的是，高频

cues.en: cosine waves don't really contribute very much to the image. For example, this one is zero, which means that this cosine wave here is having no effect on the image at all. The image is essentially not a checkerboard in any way. These ones, compared to these big coefficients here, are incredibly small as well and have very subtle effects on the actual output pixel data. I mean, these weights are so small that if you took these away,
cues.zh: 余弦波对图像其实没多大贡献。比如这个是零，说明这里的这个余弦波对图像完全没有影响。这幅图像本质上完全不是什么棋盘格。这些系数和这里这些大系数相比也小得惊人，对实际输出的像素数据只有非常细微的影响。我是说，这些权重小到如果你把它们去掉，

cues.en: the image will be almost identical.
cues.zh: 图像几乎会一模一样。

cues.en: And yet, we could just take them away and save all that space. So that's how we do it. The next step after calculating our discrete cosine transform coefficients
cues.zh: 但我们完全可以把它们去掉，省下所有这些空间。我们就是这么做的。在算出离散余弦变换系数之后，下一步

cues.en: is basically try and remove the ones we don't want. We call the process of removing the high frequency data quantization.
cues.zh: 基本上就是试着去掉我们不想要的那些。我们把去掉高频数据的过程叫作量化。

cues.en: Hopefully, it'll be easier if I show you a quantization table. This is the standard JPEG quantization table that represents a quality of 50%.
cues.zh: 如果我给你们看一张量化表，可能会更容易理解。这是标准的 JPEG 量化表，代表 50% 的质量。

cues.en: So in the JPEG standard. Different compressors like the one used in Photoshop will use different quantization tables depending on how they feel, and also what level of quality you set it at. And what we do is we divide
cues.zh: 所以在 JPEG 标准里。不同的压缩器，比如 Photoshop 里用的那个，会根据各自的做法，以及你设置的质量级别，使用不同的量化表。然后我们要做的是，把

cues.en: every one of our coefficients by the corresponding quantization value and then round to the nearest integer. Okay? And you can see already that these ones are much bigger than these ones. So what essentially happens is these get scaled by a huge amount, usually to close to zero, and then get removed by being set to zero when we round to the nearest integer. So for example,
cues.zh: 我们的每一个系数除以对应的量化值，然后四舍五入到最接近的整数。明白吗？你已经能看出来，这些比这些大得多。所以本质上会发生的是，这些会被大幅缩小，通常会接近零，然后在我们四舍五入到最近整数时被设为零，从而被去掉。比如，

cues.en: divided by 16
cues.zh: 除以 16

cues.en: is roughly 23 or minus 23. And the actual quantized output is this. You And can see that almost all of it's now zero. So this coefficient now no longer has an effect nor does this one or this one. The only ones that have any effect on our image are these nine here. And, essentially, the argument that we're making is that with just these nine, we can get pretty much the exact same image back. It won't be exactly the same. A couple of pixels will be maybe an intensity level up or down. But when viewed at a normal image range, you know, let's say a photograph on a monitor, it'll look exactly the same to us. So what we then finally do when we want to output this information into our file is we essentially list all these in a long line. We then use a Huffman encoding,
cues.zh: 大约是 23，或者 -23。而实际量化后的输出是这个。你可以看到，现在几乎所有值都是零了。所以这个系数现在不再有影响，这个和这个也一样。对我们的图像还有影响的只有这里这九个。而本质上，我们的论点是：只用这九个，我们就能得到几乎完全一样的图像。它不会一模一样。有几个像素可能会亮一档或暗一档。但在正常观看图像的距离下，你知道，比如在显示器上看一张照片，它在我们看来会完全一样。所以最后，当我们想把这些信息输出到文件里时，我们基本上就是把它们全部排成一长串。然后我们使用霍夫曼编码，

cues.en: which professor Brelford has covered in the video, to further compress this data. The way that we serialize this into our file is in a zigzag fashion. So we start with minus 23, then we go minus two, minus 21.
cues.zh: Brelford 教授在视频里已经讲过，用它来进一步压缩这些数据。我们把这些数据序列化到文件里的方式是之字形扫描。所以从 -23 开始，然后到 -2、-21。

cues.en: So we're going up and down, up and down. Six, four,
cues.zh: 我们就这样上上下下、上上下下。六、四，

cues.en: zero,
cues.zh: 零，

cues.en: zero, two, one, and so on. And the the important thing about this is by doing this, we're going to get a huge list of naughts all in a row, and that is very easily compressed by Huffman encoding. So we take this table, and we do this for every eight by eight block in our image. We then serialize them out into a long line, and we use Huffman encoding to shrink them right down, and that's what goes into our JPEG. And then all other aspects of JPEG are really sort of minor format considerations. That's the the core of how the compression works. To decompress the image, let's imagine that we've we've sent our JPEG to someone and their decoder is trying to read it. What we have to do is the exact opposite of this approach. So we begin by multiplying
cues.zh: 零、二、一，等等。这里的关键是，这样做我们会得到一长串连续的零，而霍夫曼编码非常容易压缩它。所以我们取这张表，对图像里每个 8×8 块都这样做。然后把它们序列化成一条长线，用霍夫曼编码把它们大幅缩小，这就是写进 JPEG 的内容。JPEG 的其他方面其实都只是些次要的格式考量。这就是压缩工作的核心。

cues.en: each of these values
cues.zh: 这些值中的每一个

cues.en: by our quantization table. So this is the same quantization table. It's stored inside the JPEG so we know which one they used. Because if you use a different one on the way out, you're gonna ruin your image. So we multiply each of these values
cues.zh: 乘以我们的量化表。这是同一张量化表。它存储在 JPEG 内部，所以我们知道他们用了哪一张。因为如果在解码时用了不同的表，就会毁掉图像。所以我们把每个值

cues.en: by the specific value in the quantization table, and we get the coefficients. And you can see that because most of them are naught, most of them on the other side are also naught. So none of these are going to contribute to our image anymore. Then in reverse, we use discrete cosine transform number three, which is usually just called the
cues.zh: 乘以量化表中的具体值，就得到系数。你可以看到，因为大多数都是零，另一侧的大多数也是零。所以这些都不再会贡献到我们的图像里。然后反过来，我们使用第三种离散余弦变换，通常就叫

cues.en: inverse discrete cosine transform because it's generally used to inverse what we did for discrete cosine transform two. And that gives us our shifted block back again, which, of course, we then add a 128 to every value, and we have our output block. And there it is. So that's the complete JPEG compression using discrete cosine transform. If we look at our input block and our output block next to each other...
cues.zh: 逆离散余弦变换，因为它通常用来逆转我们对第二种离散余弦变换所做的操作。这样我们就拿回了移位后的块，当然，然后给每个值加 128，就得到输出块。就是这样。这就是使用离散余弦变换的完整 JPEG 压缩。如果我们把输入块和输出块并排看……

cues.en: So there we go. We can see that there are some changes in these values, but it's actually pretty close. These have sort of changed. This has gone up a few intensity levels. This is the same. This has gone down four. But these are from naught to two five five. No one's going to see that kind of difference. And this is at 50%, so you can do a lot less than this if you have your JPEG quality set higher and smaller values in your quantization table. So in the JPEG standard, this is the quantization table that they give you. This is actually the quantization table for luminosity,
cues.zh: 就是这样。我们可以看到这些值有些变化，但其实相当接近。这些多少变了。这个升高了几个强度级别。这个没变。这个降了四。但这些是从零到 255。没人会看出这种差别。而且这是 50% 质量下，所以如果你把 JPEG 质量设得更高、量化表里的值设得更小，你可以压缩得比这少得多。所以在 JPEG 标准里，这是他们给出的量化表。这其实是亮度的量化表，

cues.en: not for chrominance. They have a different one for chrominance, which is much... Has much higher penalties
cues.zh: 不是色度的。色度有另一张表，那张表……对高频的惩罚高得多

cues.en: on the high frequency. Because if high frequency data is not very important in gray, it's even less important given that we don't see color that well. One thing you can do to immediately
cues.zh: 在高频上。因为如果高频数据在灰度中不太重要，那在我们对颜色本来就看不太清的情况下就更不重要了。你可以立即做一件事

cues.en: increase the quality of our overall JPEG compression, that is preserve as much image as possible, is to have all of these values in the quantization table.
cues.zh: 来提高整体 JPEG 压缩的质量，也就是尽可能保留图像，那就是让所有这些值都出现在量化表中。

cues.en: If we divide all of these values by two, then essentially, everything's being scaled by less. All of these high frequency coefficients won't necessarily be rounded to zero. They might be rounded to one or two, and they'll still have a little bit of an effect. On the other hand, if we increase the values in these quantization tables, we're essentially operating a lower JPEG,
cues.zh: 如果把这些值都除以二，那么本质上所有值的缩放幅度都变小了。这些高频系数不一定会被舍入到零。它们可能被舍入到一或二，仍然会有一点影响。另一方面，如果增大这些量化表中的值，本质上就是在使用更低的 JPEG，

cues.en: quality setting. This is the approach that the JPEG standard uses. In other software, they may have their own
cues.zh: 质量设置。这就是 JPEG 标准采用的方法。其他软件可能有自己的

cues.en: quantization tables. In fact, as far as I know, Photoshop... I think they have 12 quality settings, and they have different quantization tables for most of those settings and different sampling frequencies.
cues.zh: 量化表。事实上，据我所知，Photoshop……我想它有 12 个质量设置，而且其中大多数设置都有不同的量化表和不同的采样频率。

cues.en: So lots of different things that they've decided make for pretty good scale bar that a user can use. And all of those settings are all then stored in the header of the file? Yep. Between each part of them is you'll get a small block that says, these are the quantization tables and the Huffman coding tables that we used so that everyone can reverse that process. If you don't know what the quantization table was, you might be multiplying your encoded coefficients by different values and get something completely different out at the end. What what might it be? Just different colors? It could be a completely different image. You've divided by certain numbers. You need to multiply again by those numbers to reverse the process. Otherwise, you might get nonsense back out. So going back to the original diagram that I drew, this is sort of the overview of JPEG. We start with our image. We've transformed our color, and then our DCT
cues.zh: 所以他们决定了很多不同的东西，组合成用户可用的相当好用的调节刻度。那所有这些设置都会存到文件头里？对。在它们每一部分之间，你会得到一个小块，说明这些是我们用到的量化表和霍夫曼编码表，这样大家都能逆向这个过程。如果你不知道量化表是什么，就可能用不同的值去乘已编码系数，最后得到完全不同的东西。会是什么？只是颜色不同？可能是完全不同的图像。你除以了某些数，就需要再乘回那些数来逆转过程。否则可能还原出乱码。回到我画的原图，这大致就是 JPEG 的概览。我们从图像开始，先做颜色变换，然后我们的 DCT

cues.en: essentially
cues.zh: 基本上

cues.en: removes the high frequency information in our image. So if we've got an image where lots of high frequency information,
cues.zh: 去除了图像中的高频信息。所以如果一张图里有很多高频信息，

cues.en: high frequency pixel changes are happening, that might get significantly compressed, but it might also look worse. Okay? But if... But in most photographs, certainly over an eight by eight image block, you won't be finding that much high frequency information, and so we can quite safely get rid of a lot of it. We calculate our DCT coefficients. We quantize them to remove the high frequency ones, and then we use Huffman encoding to compress that into a manageable small stream that we put into our JPEG file. And then the reverse of that process is exactly that. We decode
cues.zh: 高频像素变化在发生，那它可能会被大幅压缩，但也可能看起来更差。对吧？但如果……不过大多数照片里，特别是在 8×8 的图像块上，你不会找到那么多高频信息，所以我们可以相当安全地去掉很多。我们计算 DCT 系数，量化以去掉高频部分，然后用霍夫曼编码把它压缩成可管理的小数据流，写进 JPEG 文件。然后逆向过程正好相反。我们解码

cues.en: the Huffman tables, the Huffman encoding.
cues.zh: 霍夫曼表、霍夫曼编码。

cues.en: We unquantize by multiplying by all our values in the quantization table, and then we apply the inverse DCT to obtain our block back. And we do this for every little eight by eight image in our in our picture. If our image isn't a multiple of eight,
cues.zh: 我们通过乘以量化表中的所有值来反量化，然后应用逆 DCT 还原出图像块。我们对图片中的每个 8×8 小图像都这样做。如果图像尺寸不是 8 的倍数，

cues.en: then we have to add some padding bytes at the end to make it work. Usually, we could duplicate the ones near the edge so that it kind of had... Is coherent,
cues.zh: 那就必须在末尾加一些填充字节才能处理。通常可以复制边缘附近的像素，让它……保持连贯，

cues.en: or you might do something a little bit smarter.
cues.zh: 或者你可以做得更聪明一点。

cues.en: Text violates our assumptions that high frequency information doesn't contribute a lot to the image. So this is a small eight by eight image. This is, in a sense, text. This is the computer file c with its little triangular brackets.
cues.zh: 文本打破了我们的假设，即高频信息对图像的贡献不大。这是一个 8×8 的小图像。从某种意义上说，这就是文本。这是那个带有小尖括号的计算机文件 c。
